steps.label: Do Now: Repeat the Rule
steps.content:
Do Now: Repeat the Rule

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is it easy to lose count when you repeat a rule many times?Show the answer

You have to remember which turn you are on. Writing every number down stops you from losing your place.

A warm-up puzzle. There is no code yet: follow each rule exactly.

Total: 2 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: repeat a rule

steps.text: A similar puzzle: start with 2. Triple it, then take away 1. Do this 3 times.
Turn 2 starts from the new number: 5 × 3 = 15, then 14.
Turn 3: 14 × 3 = 42, then 41. That was the third turn, so stop: the answer is 41.
Counting in steps: count from 1 to 15 in steps of 4. Write every number you say.
The next one would be 17. That is past 15, so stop. You said 4 numbers.
Now do your puzzle the same way: one turn at a time, and write every number down.
steps.visual: one turn → write it → next turn

steps.label: What Does This Program Do? Loops
steps.content:
ACSL Junior Contest 2

What Does This Program Do? Loops

Competition

  • Today: read ACSL pseudocode, follow FOR and WHILE loops, and find what a program outputs.
  • Every time, ask why: why does the loop stop there? Why is that the output?
  • Activities: a trace table race, then contest-length programs.
Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a contest ask what a program outputs, instead of asking you to write one?Show the answer

Reading code exactly is a skill on its own. If you can follow every line, you can find bugs and check your own programs.

steps.label: Reading ACSL Pseudocode
steps.content:
Reading ACSL Pseudocode

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does this program output? Why does line 3 not change a?Show the worked answer

It outputs TRUE.

== asks a question: is a equal to 8? A single = stores a value. Line 3 only asks, so a stays 8.

01  a = 5 : b = 3
02  a = a + b
03  OUTPUT a == 8
CodeMeaning
a = 5store 5 in a
a == 5is a equal to 5? TRUE or FALSE
a = 5 : b = 3two statements on one line
a != bis a not equal to b?
OUTPUT ashow the value of a
  • = stores. == compares.
  • A colon : separates statements on the same line.
  • Keywords can be in capitals or small letters.

steps.label: Operators and Functions
steps.content:
Operators and Functions

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is 2 + 3 * 4 ^ 2? Why is it not 400?Show the worked answer

It is 50. The power goes first: 4 ^ 2 = 16. Then 3 * 16 = 48. Then 2 + 48 = 50.

400 comes from working left to right, which ignores the order.

CodeValueWhat it does
7 / 23.5real division
7 % 21remainder
int(7 / 2)3whole number part
2 ^ 38power (also written 2 ↑ 3)
abs(3 - 8)5distance from 0
sqrt(16)4square root
  • Order: ! first, then ^, then * / %, then + -, then comparisons, then && and ||.
  • The same level goes left to right.
  • / keeps the decimal part. int() drops it.

steps.label: Check: Operators
steps.content:
Check: Operators

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does 9 % 3 give 0?Show the answer

3 goes into 9 exactly three times. Nothing is left over, so the remainder is 0.

Work out each value.

Total: 4 marks

steps.label: FOR Loops
steps.content:
FOR Loops

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is output? Why does the loop stop after i = 4?Show the worked answer

It outputs 10: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.

After i = 4, NEXT makes i = 5. That is past the end value 4, so the loop stops.

01  s = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 4
03    s = s + i
04  NEXT i
05  OUTPUT s
  • FOR i = 1 TO 4 gives i the values 1, 2, 3, 4 in turn.
  • The lines between FOR and NEXT run once for each value.
  • NEXT i adds 1 to i and goes back to the top.

steps.label: Compare: STEP Up and STEP Down
steps.content:
Compare: STEP Up and STEP Down

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the third loop stop at 9, not at 10?Show the answer

i goes 1, 5, 9. The next value is 13, which is past 10, so the loop stops.

The end value is a limit. The loop does not have to land on it.

LoopValues of i
FOR i = 1 TO 9 STEP 21, 3, 5, 7, 9
FOR i = 5 TO 1 STEP -15, 4, 3, 2, 1
FOR i = 1 TO 10 STEP 41, 5, 9
  • STEP 2 adds 2 each time. Without STEP, it adds 1.
  • STEP -1 counts down. The loop stops when i goes below the end value.
  • Work out the start, the end and the step once, at the start of the loop.

steps.label: Check: FOR and STEP
steps.content:
Check: FOR and STEP

Think → Pair → ShareFOR i = 1 TO 5 STEP 2: why does the body run three times?Show the answer

i takes the values 1, 3 and 5. The next value, 7, is past 5.

01  t = 0
02  FOR k = 2 TO 11 STEP 3
03    t = t + k
04  NEXT k
05  OUTPUT t
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Activity 1: Trace Table Race
steps.content:
Activity 1: Trace Table Race

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a trace table get a new row only when a value changes?Show the answer

The table records what the program does. A row shows the moment a variable gets a new value, so you can follow every step.

The program runs one step at a time. Type each new value before it is shown, then press Enter. One try for each value: keep your streak going.

steps.label: Compare: Total and Counter
steps.content:
Compare: Total and Counter

Think → Pair → Sharei goes up to 7. Why does c end at 5, not 7?Show the answer

c adds 1 each time the loop runs. The loop runs for i = 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7: that is 5 times.

s adds i itself, so s ends at 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 25.

Line inside FOR i = 3 TO 7NameWhat it addsAt the end
s = s + ia total (accumulator)adds the value of i25
c = c + 1a counteradds 1 every time5
  • A total starts at 0 and adds a value each time round.
  • A counter starts at 0 and adds 1 each time round.
  • A product starts at 1, because times 0 would always give 0.

steps.label: WHILE Loops
steps.content:
WHILE Loops

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is output? Why does the loop stop when x is 96?Show the worked answer

It outputs 5. x goes 6, 12, 24, 48, 96.

The condition x < 50 is checked at the top. 96 < 50 is FALSE, so the loop stops.

01  x = 3 : c = 0
02  WHILE x < 50
03    x = x * 2
04    c = c + 1
05  END WHILE
06  OUTPUT c
  • WHILE cond repeats the lines up to END WHILE while the condition is TRUE.
  • The condition is checked at the top, before each turn.
  • Something inside must change, or the loop never stops.

steps.label: Compare: How Many Times?
steps.content:
Compare: How Many Times?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the loop run 0 times when x starts at 60?Show the answer

The condition is checked before the first turn. 60 < 50 is FALSE, so the lines inside never run.

A FOR loop like FOR i = 5 TO 1 (no STEP) also runs 0 times.

01  x = ? : c = 0
02  WHILE x < 50
03    x = x * 2
04    c = c + 1
05  END WHILE
06  OUTPUT c
x starts atOutput (c)
35
301
600
  • FOR: you can count the turns before it starts.
  • WHILE: it runs until the condition is FALSE. It may run 0 times.

steps.label: Check: WHILE
steps.content:
Check: WHILE

Think → Pair → Sharen = 52. Why does int(n / 10) give 5?Show the answer

52 / 10 is 5.2, and int() drops the .2. Dividing by 10 and taking int() removes the last digit.

01  n = 365 : s = 0
02  WHILE n > 0
03    s = s + n % 10
04    n = int(n / 10)
05  END WHILE
06  OUTPUT s
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Does k Divide x?
steps.content:
Does k Divide x?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does int() change 2.4 but not 4?Show the answer

int() drops the decimal part. 4 has no decimal part, so it stays 4. 2.4 becomes 2.

So x / k == int(x / k) is TRUE only when x / k is a whole number: k divides x exactly.

x / kvalueint(x / k)x / k == int(x / k)
12 / 344TRUE
12 / 52.42FALSE
12 / 433TRUE
12 / 71.714285714291FALSE
  • x / k == int(x / k) is TRUE when k divides x exactly.
  • x % k == 0 tests the same thing.
  • Inside FOR k = 1 TO x, it finds the factors of x.

steps.label: Check: Count the Factors
steps.content:
Check: Count the Factors

Think → Pair → Sharen = 21. Why do k = 3 and k = 7 both count?Show the answer

3 × 7 = 21, so 21 / 3 and 21 / 7 are both whole numbers. Factors come in pairs.

01  n = 18 : c = 0
02  FOR k = 1 TO n
03    IF n / k == int(n / k) THEN
04      c = c + 1
05    END IF
06  NEXT k
07  OUTPUT c
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Nested Loops
steps.content:
Nested Loops

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is output? Why is it not 3 + 4?Show the worked answer

It outputs 12.

The inner loop runs all 4 times for each value of i. 3 values of i × 4 values of j = 12.

01  c = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 3
03    FOR j = 1 TO 4
04      c = c + 1
05    NEXT j
06  NEXT i
07  OUTPUT c
ipairs (i, j) the inner loop runs
1(1, 1) (1, 2) (1, 3) (1, 4)
2(2, 1) (2, 2) (2, 3) (2, 4)
3(3, 1) (3, 2) (3, 3) (3, 4)
  • The inner loop starts again from the beginning every time the outer loop turns.
  • Same size every time: outer turns × inner turns.

steps.label: Compare: j = 1 and j = i
steps.content:
Compare: j = 1 and j = i

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does changing FOR j = 1 TO 4 into FOR j = i TO 4 give 9, not 12?Show the answer

Now the inner loop starts at i, so it gets shorter each time: 4, then 3, then 2 turns.

4 + 3 + 2 = 9. You cannot just multiply.

01  c = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 3
03    FOR j = i TO 4
04      c = c + 1
05    NEXT j
06  NEXT i
07  OUTPUT c
iinner loopturns
1FOR j = 1 TO 44
2FOR j = 2 TO 43
3FOR j = 3 TO 42
  • When the inner loop uses i, count its turns for each i.
  • Then add them up.

steps.label: Check: Nested Loops
steps.content:
Check: Nested Loops

Think → Pair → ShareFOR i = 1 TO 2 with FOR j = 1 TO i inside: why does the inner body run 3 times?Show the answer

For i = 1 it runs once. For i = 2 it runs twice. 1 + 2 = 3.

01  s = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 3
03    FOR j = 1 TO i
04      s = s + j
05    NEXT j
06  NEXT i
07  OUTPUT s
Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Trace Fast: Spot the Pattern
steps.content:
Trace Fast: Spot the Pattern

Think → Pair → ShareThis program runs over 100 steps. Why is spotting the pattern faster than a trace table here?Show the worked answer

The inner loop adds i, i times: that is i × i. So a = 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36 = 91.

The last loop counts the factors of 91. In pairs: 1 × 91 and 7 × 13. So it outputs 4.

01  a = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 6
03    FOR j = 1 TO i
04      a = a + i
05    NEXT j
06  NEXT i
07  c = 0
08  FOR k = 1 TO a
09    IF a / k == int(a / k) THEN c = c + 1
10    END IF
11  NEXT k
12  OUTPUT c
If you seeIt means
adds i, i timesi × i
s = s + i for i = 1 to n1 + 2 + ... + n
x / k == int(x / k)k is a factor of x
a count of factorslist factors in pairs
  • First ask: what does each loop do? Say it in words.
  • Trace a few turns to check your idea. Then use it.

steps.label: Activity 2: Predict the Output
steps.content:
Activity 2: Predict the Output

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the replay show only the first and the last rows?Show the answer

The full trace has hundreds of rows. The start shows the pattern, and the end shows the answer.

Contest-length programs. You get one try at each output. Then watch the trace and the pattern.

steps.label: Practice: Contest Style (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Practice: Contest Style (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareUp to 30, how would you count the numbers that are multiples of 2 or of 5, without listing them all?Show the answer

Count the multiples of 2 and of 5, then take away the multiples of 10, because they were counted twice.

Contest style: one answer. Spot the pattern before you trace.

01  c = 0
02  FOR i = 1 TO 60
03    IF i % 4 == 0 || i % 6 == 0 THEN c = c + 1
04    END IF
05  NEXT i
06  OUTPUT c
Total: 1 mark

steps.label: Practice: Contest Style (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Practice: Contest Style (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareFOR k = 30 TO 1 STEP -9: why is the last value of k 3?Show the answer

k goes 30, 21, 12, 3. The next value, -6, is below 1, so the loop stops.

01  s = 0 : n = 0
02  FOR k = 50 TO 1 STEP -7
03    s = s + k
04    n = n + 1
05  NEXT k
06  OUTPUT s / n
Total: 2 marks

steps.label: Try the Real Sample
steps.content:
Try the Real Sample

Think → Pair → ShareWhy practise on a real past paper before the contest?Show the answer

You see how the questions are written and how long they take. Nothing on the day is a surprise.

ACSL publishes a sample Junior Contest 2. Try its What Does This Program Do? question on paper, then check it with your class.

  • ACSL Junior Contest 2 sample (PDF)
  • ACSL wiki: What Does This Program Do? (rules and more examples)
  • Use what you learned today: say what each loop does, trace a few turns, then spot the pattern.

steps.label: Plenary: Loops Drill
steps.content:
Plenary: Loops Drill

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does each card give you a new program every time?Show the answer

You cannot remember the answer, so you have to trace it. That is the skill the contest tests.

Operators, FOR and STEP, WHILE, nested loops and the int() test. Every program is new each time. Your progress is saved.

acl_do_now.feedback: Write down the number after every turn. Each turn starts from the last number.
Write the numbers: 2, 5, ... Stop before you pass 20. Then count them.

acl_check_operators.feedback: / is real division: keep the decimal part.
% gives the remainder. How many are left after taking out all the 4s?
Work out 17 / 4 first. Then int() drops the decimal part.

acl_check_for.feedback: Write the values of k: start at 2 and add 3. Stop before you pass 11.
Add up every value that k takes.
Count down from 20 in fives. Stop before you go below 1.

acl_check_while.feedback: 365 / 10 is 36.5. int() drops the decimal part.
Keep going until n is 0. Count the turns.
n % 10 is the last digit. s adds up the digits.

acl_check_divisible.feedback: Work out 18 / 4. Is it a whole number?
c counts every k that divides 18 exactly. List them in pairs: 1 and 18, ...
List the factors of 16 in pairs. One pair is the same number twice.

acl_check_nested.feedback: For each i, the inner loop runs i times. Add them up.
For each i, add 1 + 2 + ... + i. Then add those totals.
Now each turn adds i, and there are i turns. What does that make for each i?

acl_practice.feedback: Count the multiples of 4 and the multiples of 6 up to 60. Some numbers are both: count them once.

acl_practice_2.feedback: Write the values of k: 50, 43, ... Stop before you go below 1.
Add up the values of k, then divide by n. / keeps the decimal part.
